key_insight: Referral text strongly shifted multimodal LLM decisions between glioma and brain abscess, outweighing MRI evidence in this study.
clinical_relevance: For AI-assisted brain imaging interpretation, referral wording may bias classification, and instructions to ignore it did not reliably resolve the problem.
method: Retrospective single-center study of 60 MRI examinations: 30 gliomas and 30 abscesses.
Four multimodal LLMs assessed one axial slice per case with five referral texts and three prompt instructions.
Repeated queries yielded 72,000 answers; two blinded radiologists assessed images without referral text.
evidence_signal: Changing referral text shifted tumor-call frequency by 79–100 percentage points; model accuracy was 52–73%, versus 78% and 73% for radiologists.
watch_item: The small, single-center, single-slice evaluation limits generalizability; this was a diagnostic AI study, not cancer drug discovery research.
paper_title: Clinical referral text overrides MRI evidence in multimodal large language models: glioma versus brain abscess
